pages.title: Highly available web application on AWS, cost-optimised

finalAnswer:
Modelled, rendered, all gates passed: [Cost-optimised HA web app on AWS](<temp>\project\.archi-made-easy\architecture-cost-optimized-20261110-230500\cost-optimized.html)

**$1,108.48 → $498.92/month (−55%), with composite availability unchanged at 99.85%.** Your `solution.*` files are untouched; this is a new document.

The model priced your baseline at $1,108.48, concentrated in two places: the Fargate per-request charge ($420.48) and the Aurora instance ($410). Everything reaching Aurora and Fargate was paying full origin price because nothing was cached at the edge, and both data tiers were running at roughly a quarter of their declared capacity.

| Lever | Saving/mo | What it costs you |
|---|---|---|
| CloudFront serves 70% at the edge (`cdn→lb` multiplier 0.3) | −$294.34 | Needs cacheable responses and correct cache headers |
| Aurora right-sized (1,500 → 800 rps capacity) | −$200.00 | Less burst headroom at the DB |
| Fargate on ARM64 (task base and per-request rate) | −$53.22 | ARM-compatible image required |
| ElastiCache right-sized (50,000 → 12,000 rps) | −$62.00 | Smaller hot set before eviction pressure |

Side effects are favourable, not just neutral: critical-path P99 drops 308 ms → 260 ms and max sustainable load rises 1,000 → 2,000 rps, because the origin now carries less traffic.

**Trade-offs made explicit.** I kept every redundancy property — zone spread on all tiers, and the two-task Fargate floor. That floor is why the review score moved 82 → 81: it opens a "idle capacity kept running" finding, which is the deliberate price of surviving a zone failure. Three priced alternatives are loaded in the diagram's Workbench so you can switch between them:

- **Smaller Fargate tasks** — $442.92 (−$56), availability unchanged, P99 +17 ms. The best remaining cut, and it closes the idle-capacity finding.
- **One Fargate task** — $442.92 (−$56) but availability 99.85% → 99.80% and a third SPOF. Same saving as above for strictly worse reliability; don't take this one.
- **Aurora with a standby** — $708.92 (+$210). Not a saving, but the best reliability buy here: it closes your highest-severity finding and lifts the score to 90.

Worth knowing: **removing ElastiCache costs $172 more, not less**, because every read falls back to Aurora and the larger instance comes back. The cache is paying for itself.

Both single points of failure (Aurora, Cognito) are unchanged — I didn't make reliability worse to get the cost down, but I didn't fix them either, since both fixes add cost.

Caveats on the numbers: these are an analytical model of the declared design, not measurements or quotes. The prices and instance tiers I set are illustrative design targets — re-run with figures from your actual bill before committing. Only 4 of 10 components carry cost data, so CloudFront data transfer, S3, SQS, Lambda and Cognito are absent from both the before and the after; CDN egress in particular is a real line the model cannot see. A Compute Savings Plan would cut the rates further without any architectural change, but it locks in one to three years, so I left it out of the design and recorded it as a rejected option in the ADR.
